You are doing READ-ONLY research using the mcp-atlassian Confluence tools (confluence_search, confluence_get_page, confluence_get_page_children, confluence_get_space_page_tree, etc.). Do NOT create, edit, or delete any Confluence content.

Context: This is for the "Zimmermann PWA Kit" project, a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront. The Confluence space key is `SFCC` (base URL https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/), root page "SFCC Migration" (id 241434627).

Goal: find every software-engineering "harness" or "guardrail" documented in Confluence — i.e. process/automation gates that enforce quality, security, or release safety (CI/CD gates, review/approval requirements, QA pipeline stages, branching/release rules, security/compliance gates, environment setup gates) — as opposed to general product/design documentation (skip Figma/UX/design-tracker content, skip integration TSD content unless it describes a *safety/approval gate* rather than functional design).

Please specifically read and extract guardrail details from these known pages (fetch each with confluence_get_page, get the full body):

1. **304840733 — Branching Guide (GitFlow)** — extract exact approval counts required per branch type, release tagging script/process, any merge restrictions.
2. **305561601 — PWA CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions)** — extract the pipeline stages, what gates exist, required checks.
3. **304840754 — SIT Quality Gates** — extract exact thresholds and the secrets/credentials list mentioned (names only, not values).
4. **277544962 (parent) + child guides 277577757, 277708807, 277676053, 305528833 — AI-Assisted QA six-stage pipeline** — extract the six stages (Story→AC→Zephyr→Playwright→BrowserStack→Triage) with a one-line description of what gate/check each stage represents.
5. **261750785 — Development Standards** and **261881857 — Component Override Strategy** — extract any process/review guardrails mentioned (not day-to-day code style — focus on review requirements, approval gates, anything enforced rather than just convention).
6. **259358732 / 259686402 / 268337165 / 305430530 — 7.1 Platform & Tool Access / 7.1a Tracker / 7.1b Third-Party Credentials / 7.1c CI-CD & Env Setup Checklist** — extract what access-control or credential-handling gates exist.
7. **256835585 — Technical Solution Design – PWA** — extract ONLY the guardrail-relevant sections: env-var security table, Didomi consent-gate table (what must gate on consent), and any stated SSR/CSR security boundaries. Skip general architecture description.
8. Do a `confluence_search` for terms like "approval", "gate", "required reviewer", "branch protection", "security review", "compliance", "sign-off", "checklist" within the SFCC space to catch anything not in the list above (e.g. under the 05.3 Integration section or elsewhere). Report any additional pages found with a one-line summary of the guardrail they document.

For each item, cite the page title and ID. Report back in a structured format matching the 8 numbered categories above (plus a 9th for any additional pages found in step 8). Use bullet points with concrete extracted facts (exact numbers, names, thresholds) — not prose paraphrase. If a page can't be fetched or doesn't exist anymore, say so explicitly rather than guessing its content. This report feeds into a comprehensive guardrails document, so accuracy matters — do not invent details that aren't actually in the page body.

Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

# Confluence Guardrails Audit — SFCC Space

All pages fetched successfully (read-only; no edits made). Findings below, organized per the 8 requested categories plus a 9th for additional discoveries from the search step.

---

## 1. Branching Guide (GitFlow) — page 304840733

**Approval counts per branch:**
- `feature/*` → `develop`: **1 approval** required ("develop is a shared integration point")
- `fix/*` → `develop`: same as feature (1 approval, via `qa.yml` unit tests)
- `hotfix/*` → `main` **and** `develop`: approvals not stated on this page (see CI/CD page: 2)
- `release/**`: created by squad leads/CI from a tagged `develop` state — developers do not create these directly
- `fix/release-{version}-*` → `release/**`: PR back into the release branch; squad leads separately apply the same fix to `develop` via a second PR
- Direct commits to a release branch: only for **no-logic changes** (copy corrections, version bumps, boolean flag toggles) — require **explicit squad lead approval**

**Release tagging process:** `scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version}` run from `main` after the release PR merges — creates both `v{version}` and `release/digital/v{version}` git tags. Sprint boundary tags (`sprint/{N}/{date}`) are created automatically by CI when `scripts/sprint.txt` is updated.

**Version format:** Pre-go-live `v0.{sprint}.0`; go-live `v1.0.0`; post-launch patches `v1.0.{patch}`; post-launch features `v1.{minor}.0`.

**Merge restrictions:** Claude Code is "physically blocked" from writing to `develop`/`main` via a branch-lock hook in `.claude/settings.json`. On `release/**`, Claude Code runs in supervised/read-only-skills mode; code logic fixes must go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch.

---

## 2. PWA CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions) — page 305561601

**Trigger matrix (workflow → jobs):**
- Push to `develop` → `digital-sit.yml`: install → playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size → sit-gate → deploy-sit → tag-sit-deploy, tag-sprint
- PR → `release/**` → `digital-sit.yml`: install → four signal jobs → sit-gate (no deploy)
- PR → `develop` or `release/**` → `qa.yml`: unit-tests, storybook-test (every PR) → e2e-browserstack (release/** only)
- PR opened (any branch) → `protected-file-guard.yml`: tier-1-guard, tier-2-guard
- Weekly cron (Mon 1am UTC) → `weekly-agents.yml`: quality-sweep, contentful-drift-audit, changelog-reminder
- Weekly cron (Mon 0:00 UTC) → `upstream-release-watch.yml`: check-for-new-release

**Branch protection — required approvals:**
- `develop`: **2 approvals** (one owning squad, one cross-squad), required status check `unit-tests`, branches must be up to date, no bypass
- `main`: **2 approvals** (both squad leads), same up-to-date/no-bypass rules; hotfix PRs into `main` still require 2 approvals
- `release/**`: required check = `Digital SIT Gate` composite job

**Digital SIT Gate thresholds (also gates `release/**` merges):**
| Signal | Tool | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| Playwright P0 | Playwright | 100% pass, all storefront configs |
| Lighthouse CI | LHCI | Perf ≥80, A11y ≥90, Best Practices ≥90; >5pt drop = blocked |
| MuleSoft contract tests | Pact/OpenAPI | Any schema breach = blocked (pending spec source) |
| Bundle size | bundlewatch | main.js <180kB, vendor.js <250kB, main.css <50kB |

**STAGE convergence gate:** manual, not a GitHub status check — checklist: Digital SIT Gate green + NewStore SIT complete + Integration Lead and both squad leads signed off.

**Commit message enforcement:** Layer 1 = local `commit-msg` Husky hook (types: feat/fix/docs/style/refactor/perf/test/build/ci/chore/upstream-sync). Layer 2 = CodeRabbit PR review (`coderabbit.yaml`).

**CI Secrets (names only):** `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`, `LHCI_TOKEN`, `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT`, `MRT_USER`, `MRT_API_KEY`, `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME`, `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY`, `RETAIL_APP_HOME_SIT`, `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL`, `PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, `E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER`.

---

## 3. SIT Quality Gates — page 304840754

- Four automated checks gate promotion to `release/**` — enforced by GitHub branch protection; cannot merge without green `Digital SIT Gate`.
- **Thresholds** (same as above): Playwright P0 100% pass; Lighthouse Perf ≥80/A11y ≥90/Best Practices ≥90 (>5pt drop blocks); bundle main.js<180kB/vendor.js<250kB/main.css<50kB; contract tests = any breach blocks.
- Playwright `retries` intentionally set to **0** — flaky tests must be fixed, not retried away.
- **Open dependency:** `test:contracts` currently exits 0 with a warning — not a real assertion yet (owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead).
- **Secrets:** `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`, `LHCI_TOKEN`, `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` (Lighthouse); `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME`, `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY`, `RETAIL_APP_HOME_SIT`, all `E2E_*` SKU secrets (BrowserStack, `qa.yml` on `release/**` PRs only, Chrome/Safari/Firefox/Edge).

---

## 4. AI-Assisted QA Six-Stage Pipeline — pages 277544962 (parent), 277577757, 277708807, 277676053, 305528833

| Stage | Gate/check represented |
|---|---|
| 1 — Story Intake | BA structures Jira story to a fixed template (role, goal, in/out of scope, regions, edge cases) — no gate yet, but poor input here degrades every downstream stage |
| 2 — AC Authoring with Claude | **HUMAN GATE 1**: BA must review every AC line and set Jira status to "AC Approved" before Zephyr work begins |
| 3 — Zephyr Test Case Creation via MCP | **HUMAN GATE 2**: Tester reviews steps/expected results and marks each case "Ready for Execution"; nothing is created in Zephyr before review |
| 4 — Playwright Spec Authoring | Developer replaces placeholder selectors in Page Object files and confirms the spec passes locally before commit — no formal human gate but a mandatory manual step |
| 5 — BrowserStack Execution | GitHub Actions triggers BrowserStack on PR to `release/**`; matrix = 7 storefronts × 4 browsers (28 parallel contexts); results auto-sync to Zephyr |
| 6 — Defect Triage & Fix Branch | **HUMAN GATE 3**: agent classifies failures (code defect/env/test-data), tier-gates its own actions (Tier 1 = stop + Jira defect only; Tier 2 = fix + PR + second-reviewer label; Tier 3–4 = full auto-fix + PR); no PR is ever merged without human code review |

Additional detail: P0 specs (`.p0.spec.{ts,js}`) run in the SIT gate on merge to `develop`; `.p1`+ run in the full BrowserStack matrix on PRs to `release/**`. Selector priority enforced in code review: ARIA role+name → label → visible text → `data-testid` → never CSS class/DOM position.

---

## 5. Development Standards (261750785) & Component Override Strategy (261881857)

**Development Standards** — process/review guardrails (not style):
- File protection tiers table: **Tier 1 (Frozen)** — stop, get owner approval before any change; **Tier 2 (Protected)** — PR requires a second reviewer, notify owner; **Unclassified** — normal feature-branch workflow.
- Pre-PR gate: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test` must all pass before opening a PR.

**Component Override Strategy** — process guardrails:
- Copy-first pattern for overriding base template files: copy → convert to TS → `npx tsc --noEmit` → temporary `console.log` to verify override renders → remove log only after functional changes begin.
- "Branch first" rule: every change goes on a feature branch, never directly on `develop`/`main`.
- No formal approval/review-count guardrails beyond referring back to the Branching Guide and the tier system above.

---

## 6. 7.1 Platform & Tool Access family — pages 259358732, 259686402, 268337165, 305430530

**259358732 (7.1 Platform & Tool Access):** simple ownership table — who owns each tool (Jira/Confluence/SFCC BM/SFCC MRT/Magento/GitHub/Figma/SharePoint) and who to request access from. No gate logic beyond "request access from X."

**259686402 (7.1a Tool Access Tracker):** per-person access-confirmed/pending tracker (traffic-light Green=confirmed, Red=pending) across Jira, Confluence, SFCC BM, SFCC Sandbox, SFCC MRT, GitHub, Figma (x2 instances), Zephyr, Magento, Contentful — an access-control audit trail, not itself a gate mechanism.

**268337165 (7.1b Third Party Credentials):** vendor credential tracker — for each vendor (MuleSoft, Omneo, GiveX, Adyen, Global-e, Contentful, Narvar, Google Maps/Business, Didomi, GTM/Tell No Lies, Inside Chat, Magento, Google reCAPTCHA) lists **credential types required** (names only, e.g. "Client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID"), environments needed, and who provides them. Status column marks most as "Not yet requested" — several flagged as **hard blockers** (MuleSoft, Adyen, Global-e, Contentful, Google Maps, Didomi, GTM).

**305430530 (7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist):** the most concrete access-control gate documentation:
- Full branch protection setup instructions for `develop`/`main`/`release/*` (see §1/2 above), including the exact required-status-check strings: `🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check`, `🔴 Branch Target Check`, `🟡 Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning`, `🟡 Cross-Squad Boundary Check`.
- GitHub Teams required for CODEOWNERS: `design-system`, `integration-lead`, `squad-a-lead`, `squad-b-lead`, `squad-leads`.
- Verification step: open a test PR touching one Tier 1 file — expect the Tier 1 check to fail, other checks pass, CodeRabbit posts review, Integration Lead auto-requested, merge blocked.
- Summary protection table distinguishing **hard-fail (blocks merge)** vs **warning-only** guardrails — Tier 1 touch and wrong branch target are hard fails; Tier 2 touch and cross-squad PR are warnings only (until CODEOWNERS-enforced review kicks in).

---

## 7. Technical Solution Design – PWA — page 256835585

**§4.1 Environment Configuration — security boundary table (credential group → boundary):**
| Credential group | Boundary |
|---|---|
| SFCC Shopper API (SLAS) | Client ID browser-direct (public); token refresh MRT-mediated |
| Google Maps Places | MRT-mediated — key never reaches browser |
| Contentful Delivery | Browser + SSR — read-only token, safe in bundle |
| Contentful Preview | MRT-mediated — never reaches browser |
| Contentful Management | CI only — never deployed to MRT |
| Contentful publish webhook | MRT-mediated — HMAC-verified |
| MuleSoft | MRT-mediated — credentials never reach browser |
| Adyen | Client key browser-direct (public by design); server API in SFCC |
| Narvar | Browser-direct — public account ID |
| reCAPTCHA | Site key browser-direct (public); secret key MRT-mediated |
| Global-e | Merchant ID/script host browser-direct; server API key MRT-mediated |
| Didomi | Browser-direct — public notice ID |
| GTM/Addingwell | Browser-direct — both container ID and server URL public |
| Observability | License keys MRT-mediated; per-tier env tag browser-accessible |

Security policy: real values only in local untracked env file; committed template holds variable names only (secrets = empty value, public IDs may have placeholders); MRT variables managed per-environment in the MRT console.

**§11.4 Didomi consent-gate reference table:**
| Integration | Didomi purpose/vendor ID | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| GTM (Addingwell) | Handled by Tell No Lies in container | All storefronts |
| Inside Chat | Handled by Tell No Lies in GTM container | All storefronts |
| Optimizely Web | TBC (Analytics?) | US only |
| Crazy Egg | TBC (Analytics?) | All storefronts |
| Narvar Promise | TBC | Domestic only |
| reCAPTCHA v3 | n/a — loads on form interaction, no consent required | All except EU & UK |
| reCAPTCHA v3 | TBC | EU & UK only |
| Measmerize | TBC | PDP only |
| Vimeo | TBC (dnt=1, no consent) | PDP + editorial |
| Recently Viewed | TBC (Analytics?) | All storefronts |

Note: purpose IDs are an **open item** pending Didomi provisioning. §11.1: fail-closed policy — if consent state can't be determined, no third-party scripts load at all.

**§8.1.1 SSR vs CSR boundary table:**
| Page type | Pattern | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| PDP, PLP, content, homepages, boutique | Full SSR | Indexable, SEO/LCP-critical |
| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | SSR shell + CSR data | Personalised/behind auth; no SEO value (blocked in robots.txt); server-rendering personalised data risks state leaking across requests |
| Search results, filtered PLP | SSR shell + CSR data | Blocked in robots.txt; client-driven filter/sort |

**§12.1 Blast-Radius Containment (SSR security boundary):** each upstream origin gets its own SSR connection pool with independent concurrency cap — SFCC SCAPI (SLAS JWKS), SFCC Payments (payment method metadata), MuleSoft, Google Places, Booxi — explicitly to prevent a slow/flooded integration (e.g. checkout under load) from starving connections to unrelated origins (Contentful, SLAS JWKS). GiveX balance calls specifically flagged as carrying payment credentials and must not be queued behind other traffic.

---

## 8. Additional guardrail pages found via search

- **277708843 — TSD: AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent** — most detailed automated-agent guardrail doc found. §8 "Security & Guardrails" table: no auto-merge (branch protection on `develop`/`release/**`, cannot be bypassed by workflow/bot); Tier 1 hard stop on code generation enforced deterministically by `classify-tier.js` (a CODEOWNERS lookup, **never delegated to the LLM**); Tier 2 auto-fix permitted but PR carries `tier-2-change` label + CODEOWNERS-enforced second reviewer; credentials never placed in LLM prompt context; agent PRs carry `agent-raised` label and `fix/agent-` branch prefix; Jira writes go through a scoped service-account token (issue create/link only, no admin/bulk/cross-project); CodeRabbit reviews agent PRs same as human PRs. Uses **AWS Bedrock** (Haiku for classification, Sonnet for investigation/fix), never the Anthropic API directly from CI, since the Atlassian MCP can't run on a GitHub Actions runner.
- **305102849 — Human-in-the-Lead AI Development — Project Setup Overview** — narrative governance overview; confirms hooks (`branch-lock`, `tier2Warn.sh`, `contentfulDriftWarn.sh`, `testFileRemind.sh`), the `.claude/settings.json` permission model (reads free, writes/edits/pushes/installs/destructive commands require approval), and that `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` Husky hooks block direct edits to derived AI-config files (`.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) when their `.claude/` source isn't also staged.
- **304840708 — Environment Topology & Promotion Path** — six-tier LOCAL→DEV→SIT→STAGE→UAT→PROD topology with explicit gates per tier: DEV requires the six-signal Digital SIT Gate; STAGE requires both Digital SIT Gate green **and** NewStore OMS SIT sign-off (manual, Jira-booked); UAT requires business stakeholder sign-off per region; PROD requires release-manager manual approval gate in GitHub Environments plus AU canary (<0.5% error rate over 2h) before wider rollout. **GitHub Environment secret scope table**: `staging` (no reviewer), `sit`/`pre-prod` (Zimmermann environment owner reviewer), `uat` (Zimmermann stakeholder reviewer), `production` (Release manager reviewer) — SIT secrets explicitly must not be accessible to the `production` environment workflow.
- **278921217 — 05.5 Agent Registry** — programme-wide non-negotiable constraints for *all* AI agents: Bedrock-only (no direct Anthropic API from automated contexts), Tier 1 hard stop (deterministic CODEOWNERS check, never LLM-delegated), no auto-merge ever, human gate on all code changes, MCP for interactive writes vs REST API for CI writes (all carry `agent-raised` label), credentials in CI secrets only/never in LLM context. Also: any PR introducing a new agent file without a matching registry update is flagged by CodeRabbit and must not merge until the registry is current.
- **285540356 — 05.6 Environment Details** — SIT-specific operational guardrails: manual SIT deployments must use a `sit/*` or `hotfix/*` branch; never push to SIT from `develop`/`main` without the CI gate confirming Digital Dev is green; never enable Einstein/Global-e/Narvar on SIT; never use SIT as a hotfix path to PROD (must go `hotfix/* → main → PROD`); if SIT breaks, do not block the Digital release.
- **318472193 — Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations** — approval-gated Contentful scripts: `npm run setup:contentful` and `npm run promote:alias` require **Tier 1 approver**; `npm run config:contentful` (writes) also Tier 1 approver, read-only view open to any dev; `npm run sync:contentful` and `detect:drift` open to any developer. Drift detection (`detectDrift`) runs automatically before migrations apply (bypass via `--force`) and is usable as a CI gate (`npm run detect:drift` exits non-zero on drift found). Contentful roles restrict content-type editing on `sit`/`staging`/`uat`/`master` to the CI service account only — human editors get CRUD on entries/assets but cannot touch content types there.
- **264896514 — SFCC Build and Deployment Process – Headless Architecture** (SFCC backend, included because it's a stated approval gate rather than functional design) — "the `vendor/` folder requires approval from @mani060689 before any PR can be merged"; environment promotion (QA→Staging→Production) follows "approval gates."
- **277807105 — 05.4 QA & Testing (parent index page)** — restates the three human gates in one line: "No AC is approved without BA sign-off. No test case is created without Tester review. No PR is merged without human code review."
- **304775192 — Claude Code CLI Developer Onboarding Guide** (surfaced but not deep-fetched — indexed only) — confirms Tier 1/Tier 2 owner names live in AGENTS.md Contact Map and `.claude/rules/`.

**Pages searched for but not found needing separate fetch / not guardrail-relevant:** none of the 8 target categories were missing — all requested page IDs resolved successfully. No broken/missing pages encountered.
